desc:
A word can be abbreviated by replacing some of its non-overlapping, non-adjacent substrings by their lengths written in decimal. For example internationalization can be written as i18n (the 18 letters between i and n are replaced by 18) or as i12iz4n, which mixes letters and numbers.

Given a lowercase word and a string abbr made of lowercase letters and digits, decide whether abbr is a valid abbreviation of word. Read abbr from left to right: each lowercase letter must equal the next unread letter of the word, and each maximal run of digits is a number k that skips the next k letters of the word. The whole word has to be consumed exactly.

A number may not start with the digit 0, so it can neither have leading zeros nor be zero itself (0, 05 are invalid).

For example, word = "substitution" matches "s10n" and "sub4u4" and "12", but not "s55n" (skips too much), "s010n" (leading zero) or "s0ubstitution" (zero).
constraints: word contains lowercase letters only; abbr contains lowercase letters and digits only
every run of digits in abbr is at most 8 characters long
hints: Walk through the word and the abbreviation at the same time with two pointers.
On a letter, compare it with the current letter of the word. On a digit, read the whole run of digits as a number and advance the word pointer by that amount.
Check the special cases: a run starting with 0 is invalid, jumping beyond the end of the word is invalid, and at the end the word pointer has to be exactly at the end of the word.
editorial: Keep a pointer i into the word and a pointer j into the abbreviation. If abbr[j] is a letter, it must equal word[i] (and i must still be inside the word); then both pointers advance. If it is a digit, first reject it when it is 0 (a number cannot start with zero, which also excludes the number zero), then read the maximal digit run into the number k, and advance i by k. If i goes past the end, the abbreviation is too long.

After the abbreviation is used up, the match is valid exactly when i equals the length of the word. Each character of abbr is read once, and the digit runs are short, so the time is O(|abbr|) with O(1) extra space. Because each number is capped at 8 digits there is no overflow worry in fixed-width integers either.
